newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes subdued, WTI/Brent narrows.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes subdued, WTI/Brent narrows.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes were subdued on Friday as Gulf Coast refiners worked in last-minute domestic deals ahead of pipeline scheduling early next week, traders said.
The April spread between West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent was around $1.50-55 cents a barrel Friday afternoon, down five to 10 cents from Thursday.
Although narrower, the spread was still high enough to encourage sellers to show Brents into the Gulf Coast.
Brent for mid-April arrival was offered at April WTI minus 30 cents a barrel from the most aggressive seller, traders said.
A handful of other companies are showing first-half April barrels for around April WTI minus 20 cents, but bidders are said to be about 10 cents lower.
Meanwhile, at least two companies are showing Angolan Cabinda into the Gulf Coast. A U.S. company is offering April 5-10 delivery, asking April WTI minus 60 cents a barrel.
A broker is offering Cabinda around the same period for April WTI minus 80 cents a barrel, traders said.
